harbor_p27_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p27_001.text: The selection meeting opened late in the twenty-seventh week, while Yue's seven privately paid nights were nearly over. The three launch plans could still complete their bounded work during the remaining safe days. Han placed the public comparison on the table; protected household files stayed at their ordinary desks. The traveler entered with her personal notebook and habitual pack left secure at lodging. She had no visitor wage, official loan or inherited authority. The council had invited one unpaid recommendation from identified observations, then would confirm the chosen plan through its committee and accepting keeper.

harbor_p27_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p27_002.text: The fiscal clerk read the source aloud: one sixty-four reserved from the authorized maintenance appropriation. The old seven-hundred-sixty guarantee, permit refunds, two appointment returns, private warehouse remedies and emergency readiness were separate closed or bounded accounts. No money could be moved from them merely because a favorite plan needed more. Registry, repair and road each totaled sixty-four under current accepted quotes. The chosen keeper would order its work, verify delivery and retain receipts. The first formal review would occur four weeks after launch, closeout eight, with any unspent amount returned to the maintenance line.

harbor_p27_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p27_003.text: Han read Yue's completed appointment status only because the public summary still confused it with the pilot. The initial one hundred ninety-two had closed at one hundred forty-eight spent and forty-four returned. The new two hundred had closed after twenty-eight paid half-days at one hundred eighty-four spent and sixteen returned. All task loans and official packets were reconciled. Her personal notes, cup, bedding, ordinary blade and wrapped pendant remained hers. The private week cost fourteen for bed only, with food from her own purse or ordinary invitations. There was no hidden continuation of the visitor's contract.

harbor_p27_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p27_004.text: Sui confirmed the port's current emergency account: one hundred seventy-two spent from two hundred forty, sixty-eight left in its four categories. Eight stones had been bought, two exhausted in drill and two in storm; four unused remained secured. Their screen rating covered narrow fragments and spray, never people, tides or heat. Deren's twenty-six lost earnings, Bao's eighteen and Ke's six partial tool payment came from their respective employer liability sources, not the pilot. The captain gave the facts once, then sat down. Ordinary duty results and care continued whatever the committee selected.

harbor_p27_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p27_005.text: The maintenance chair repeated the existing-rights clause. Paid voyage wages, permit refunds, household consent boundaries and the platform findings remained effective on every route. The warehouse's private repair and loss accounts were closed with their proper returns. The packing venture's paid work and future contracts belonged to its private terms, not a public prize. A pilot could improve one service without becoming the harbor's final judgment on who mattered. Yue saw Deren relax slightly at the words. He still wanted repair. He Ming still wanted road, and Han's eyes kept returning to the cabinet drawing.

harbor_p27_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p27_006.text: Each accepting keeper answered the last launch question. Registry had its paid staff and interpreter tasks, cabinet quote and form supply. Repair had checked cover fittings, independent signoff, crew instruction and bounded follow-up. Road had two collection and two reply journeys, actual workers, safe licensed route and permitted receiving forms. None had spent the reservation early. The committee could confirm any one after Yue's recommendation, and the fiscal clerk would check the countersigned order. The traveler looked at the three drawings, then at people whose days would contain the consequences long after her private bed receipt ended.

harbor_p27_007.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p27_007.text: I prefer road. I have said why, and I know the other two answers do something real. If you recommend registry, I will complain about distance and still tell Lu Lian the existing route. If you recommend repair, I will admire a cover while wishing a boat arrived. I do not want a vote that makes people pretend their needs vanished. I want the chosen keeper to do the actual work. Yue, nobody here needs you to stay until every disappointed person learns a better expression. We need you to recommend something you can defend and then hear the answer.

harbor_p27_008.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p27_008.text: I prefer repair, and my own role limits remain whatever the choice. The fitting cannot sign its own inspection, and the pilot cannot make Deren's accident a fortunate lesson. If it wins, the independent officer checks the work before use and follows the actual result. If it loses, the required ordinary checks remain due. I have read that enough times to believe it even when I dislike waiting. Bo has supplied a joke about the cabinet inspecting our handwriting, which I refuse to endorse publicly. Ask me privately afterward if the room needs a smaller subject.

harbor_p27_009.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p27_009.text: I prefer registry. I want a person reaching this desk to find the proper reference and an actual reader during the funded hours. I also know a cabinet does not cross water and a clear index does not strengthen timber. My later reviews have ordinary coverage, including leave, and the private files stay where consent permits them. I will accept the plan that is confirmed and keep doing the clerk work whichever drawing wins. Yue, say your recommendation in your own words. I would rather argue with those than hear a sentence shaped to spare everybody's feelings.

harbor_final_choice.speaker: narrator
harbor_final_choice.text: Yue rose with the three comparisons visible and her own observed sources named. One maintenance fund could buy the index work, the inspection improvements or the scheduled returning visits. The committee had found all three eligible; its confirmation and the keeper's countersign would make one order actual. She would not select who deserved wages, care or an address, since those rights already stood. She could choose which bounded improvement to recommend from the harbor she had learned. The room waited, full of people whose preference was not an error the traveler had to correct before leaving.

choices.text: Recommend the registry and its checked receiving index.
Recommend repair and independently checked fittings.
Recommend road visits with permitted returning replies.

harbor_registry_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_001.text: Yue recommended the registry plan, naming the checked doorway, permitted public references and staffed receiving hours that had made the difference visible to her. The committee compared the source and confirmed the eligible order. Han accepted the keeper role again in words the clerk recorded. The fiscal countersign reserved all sixty-four for this plan alone; repair and road stayed unfunded proposals, with ordinary duties and existing routes continuing. He Ming breathed out sharply. Deren folded his preferred drawing. Neither was asked to applaud. Yue sat down, relieved by the clear decision and saddened by the faces it left unchanged.

harbor_registry_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_002.text: The cabinet supplier delivered the agreed secure index unit at twelve copper. Peng checked its actual fit and door swing under the accepted quote before payment, not after a crowd had learned to squeeze around it. The walking-stick claimant tried the route again by invitation under the practical check arrangement. The opening remained clear. Han placed only permitted public case references and receiving locations inside. Private household addresses, testimony and wage files stayed with their ordinary custodians. The cabinet key went to the named desk keeper and its actual leave cover. Yue touched no key as a parting privilege.

harbor_registry_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_003.text: Twelve of forms arrived under the selected order and were checked against the specification, including the large-letter explanation Li Su had requested. The supplier's receipt went with the cabinet's twelve in the pilot account. The first twenty-four was now spent on delivered physical stock. Han opened the cabinet at the funded receiving hour and a worker found the referral he needed without visiting two wrong rooms. He had to wait for a separate claim answer. The index helped him reach it. He told the clerk the improvement was smaller than the notice sounded and useful enough to thank her for.

harbor_registry_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_004.text: The translation provider completed the agreed bounded launch tasks within sixteen copper, with actual language scope and recipients identified under permissions. Li read the written explanation at her own pace while another claimant heard the spoken version she had requested. The work was checked before the sixteen payment. It did not create permanent interpretation whenever somebody knocked after hours. Han named the ordinary next route for that need. Yue listened from the public side as a private visitor after her recommendation ended. The launch had people working under its actual terms, not the traveler discovering unpaid duty by staying close.

harbor_registry_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_005.text: Twenty-four paid the checked staff time for receiving and indexing across the two launch days. The fiscal keeper compared completed intervals and duties with the approved line before payment. Cabinet twelve, forms twelve, translation sixteen and staff twenty-four totaled sixty-four, with no cash remainder and no charge to emergency or old appointment returns. Han retained the receipts and public status at the proper desk. First formal review remained four weeks after launch, closeout eight, under her accepted role and ordinary cover. The index had opened; later reliability would still require people to perform the actual reviews.

harbor_registry_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_006.text: He Ming visited at an ordinary break and found Lu Lian's permitted referral could be located in the index without exposing the protected reply. She admired that part and said she still wished the chosen fund had paid returning visits across water. Han said she understood. The conversation ended with a private invitation for tea after work, not a demand that disappointment stop being voiced. Yue watched her friends hold both views without turning the cabinet into a contest one of them had lost forever. The unselected road remained a possible future proposal requiring its own money and approval.

harbor_registry_007.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_registry_007.text: The index is here, and I am glad. I want that said without making the road need sound imaginary. I have the actual key, the cover's acceptance and the first review date. I will not write to you asking for visitor labor because the cabinet develops an ordinary problem. I may write a private letter complaining about the problem if you consent to hear it, which is a different and much less admirable arrangement. Today the first worker found the right room. Tonight I intend to paint badly in my own room and ask nobody to call the day historic.

harbor_registry_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_008.text: Deren read the registry's public launch status with the independent clerk he preferred for formal explanations. The platform's required checks and paid twenty-six remained unchanged. He asked where a future crew concern would go if its maintenance note stalled. The index pointed to the existing receiving route and current escalation, which he found practical despite preferring covers. Yan met him for lunch afterward. Their conversation concerned the cup, Bo and tomorrow's actual crew work. A new cabinet had not absolved the foreman, and a lost pilot preference had not reopened the man's earned payment.

harbor_registry_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_009.text: At North Quay Packing, the third batch continued through its acquired two-week schedule. Its forty-eight advance paid the current materials, rented interval and initial wages under the same ninety-six terms; the later balance remained due after acceptance. The venture's fourteen reserve stayed separate. Ke's paid task and Wu's canteen work continued, and An asked no departing visitor for capital again. He Ming showed Yue the cabinet referral she might use if a future private account question needed the office. Then she put it down and served the private supper the friends had agreed to buy.

harbor_registry_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_010.text: The ugly gull had returned to its adjusted hook after Peng's building visit and the private arrangement its owners accepted. Its smoke streak remained. Han inspected it as a friend and said it had survived art more successfully than her latest boat curve. An declared this the first favorable staff review it had received. They laughed around the work table. Yue bought her own food share and stayed until the workers wanted to close the room. The business would have two future batches to finish after her departure, and no part of the sixty-four had been converted into their reserve.

harbor_registry_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_011.text: Fen brought her personal learning book to the final private gathering and showed one checked practice column with pride. Luo's accepted light role and private route began after the harbor's last checks, while she remained for the apprenticeship. The kettle stayed hers by their household agreement; his ordinary fishing things would travel with him. They spoke about future receiving places under actual consent. Aning asked if the traveler would visit the account shop when she returned. Yue said she would ask first and hoped the aunt would still permit her to admire the famous stool.

harbor_registry_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_012.text: Bao and Dai joined only for the interval the care plan allowed. Bao's eighteen employer-liability payment, ordinary care and private net offers remained her actual resources, not a story the registry had purchased. She wanted to hear about the launch and then complain about a customer who expected decorative knots at plain prices. Yue listened. Ke showed the shears she owned and promised no permanent job loyalty merely because the venture had given a sound paid trial. The room contained people with choices still ahead, and the traveler could enjoy them without collecting another protected statement.

harbor_registry_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_013.text: Qin arrived with privately bought beans he openly admitted not growing. His approved shorter role had actual cover, while his garden remained ambitious and incompetent. Han teased him about the cabinet inspecting agricultural claims. He said the index would need a larger drawer for slugs. The replacement custodian laughed and defended the road he had preferred without disputing the registry's actual benefit. Their wage duties would continue under the ordinary roster. Yue drank tea from her own cup and felt the gathering growing ordinary, which made it dearer than any public farewell arranged to certify success.

harbor_registry_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_014.text: Sui came after the second officer accepted the relevant ordinary handover. Emergency sixty-eight remained with its purposes, and four unused stones with their keeper; no power or stock traveled to the lodging room for a sendoff. The captain's supervisory result and Yan's independent conditions continued after the pilot opened. She brought a sound loaf bought privately and refused accusations of cheating. Yue praised its crust, then remembered the captain had purchased it and laughed. Sui said good taste was transferable even when technical achievement was not. The evening's argument moved mercifully from records to bread.

harbor_registry_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_015.text: Before leaving the private gathering, Yue confirmed that her voluntary presentation was finished and no launch task required her return. All official files and office loans were already with keepers. She collected only her personal notebook and cup from the private table. Han walked her to lodging and helped check the habitual pack by invitation: bedding, cup, notes, ordinary blade and wrapped pendant, plus privately bought road food to consume. No cabinet key, harbor stone, portrait board, loaned tool or official authority entered it. The stage-four record remained her actual current stage, with no hidden promotion tucked into the farewell.

harbor_registry_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_016.text: The licensed onward route was open under its ordinary notice. Yue bought the cart and connecting passage from her own earned purse, accepting the travel sequence rather than an escort or promised kiln job. The seven privately paid bed nights had their own closeout, and meals had been private purchases or invitations. At the morning's doorway, Han said she would send no letter until Yue supplied a receiving place she could actually share. Yue agreed, then hugged her without trying to make the arrangement stand between their bodies. The clerk held her tightly enough to make the road feel real.

harbor_registry_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_registry_017.text: At the departure stand, He Ming complained once more that road visits would have been her choice. Then she gave Yue the ordinary goodbye they both wanted. Deren admired the registry's practical route and still favored covers; Yan remained under the finding's actual roles. Fen stayed for her apprenticeship, Luo prepared his separate later cart, and Wu went back to her children and canteen. Nobody became a compulsory companion. Yue boarded with the habitual pack and her private fare, watching the harbor's named people grow small while its index keeper opened a desk that had work of its own.

harbor_end_registry.speaker: narrator
harbor_end_registry.text: Six weeks after the harbor's final checks, Yue reached the kiln town by paid carts, walking and licensed ferries. Cold had begun to sharpen the morning air. She carried the habitual pack, personal notes, remaining earned money and a fourth-stage record, with no harbor equipment or promised commission. The registry's later reviews belonged to Han and the accepted ordinary cover; Yue had made no paid claim to attend them. Inside the common firing hall she asked where a traveler could learn the actual work terms. She waited for the local answer.
harbor_end_registry.ending: A Name at the Proper Window

harbor_repair_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_001.text: Yue chose the repair plan. She described the repeated trouble at the cover edge, the difficult return path and the difference between a report heard once and a fault checked after installation. The maintenance committee confirmed the eligible order; its fiscal clerk and assigned technical keeper countersigned the single sixty-four allocation. Han tucked the cabinet proposal away. He Ming pressed her lips together. Deren did not smile immediately. He asked whether the repair would still be inspected by somebody who had not fitted it, and the keeper answered yes before anyone began celebrating.

harbor_repair_002.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_repair_002.text: I will help prepare the crew instruction, Yan said, but the present limits on my unsupervised duties continue. The repair choice does not cancel the platform finding. He stopped looking at Deren when he said it, making the words a statement to the room. The assigned officer, rather than Yan, accepted the technical signoff. Deren pulled the drawing toward himself and traced the place where his boot had caught. He wanted the edge examined while somebody actually carried a load. The officer arranged the trial with ordinary workers, light test bundles and a clear stopping signal.

harbor_repair_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_003.text: The smith arrived during the first safe launch day carrying the measured covers and fittings ordered for twenty-eight copper. They were modest pieces, dull at the edges and carefully marked underneath. A boy expected a glittering new platform and seemed offended by so much plain iron. The smith invited him to lift a spare offcut, then rescued his toes before he proved anything. The delivered pieces were checked against the order and fitted under the assigned officer's supervision. Payment followed the accepted delivery and work. Nobody treated the metal's weight as permission to load it.

harbor_repair_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_004.text: Sixteen copper paid the quoted ordinary checks across the two launch days. Workers inspected the fitted edges, the fastening points, the walking clearance and the return path, then repeated the relevant carrying trial with a manageable bundle. Deren watched from the resting place provided for his recovering leg. He asked for a second pass when the first carrier unconsciously took the easier side. That pass showed a low fastening head catching loose wrapping. The fitter corrected it before acceptance. The officer marked the correction and watched another pass rather than signing over the troublesome movement.

harbor_repair_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_005.text: The twelve-copper instruction purchase covered the completed crew report session, its practical demonstration and the checked receiving instructions. Workers rehearsed stopping a task, reaching the responsible desk and keeping the rejected load clear of the passage. Yan demonstrated without turning the exercise into a defense of himself. Sui interrupted once to ask who covered the desk when its usual keeper stepped away. The named cover answered from the bench. A carter then asked the same question in less polite language, and received the same answer. The clerk paid for the completed session, not future attendance.

harbor_repair_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_006.text: Eight copper bought the bounded followup after installation, completed before the second launch day closed. Its checker returned after ordinary use, looked for shifting fittings and heard the workers' reports with the assigned officer present. One packing strip had fallen into the passage; it was cleared, and its source addressed without blaming the new cover. The checker recorded the actual limits of the visit. The four accepted purchases were twenty-eight, sixteen, twelve and eight: sixty-four spent, no remaining pilot cash. The separate four-week and eight-week reviews stayed on the ordinary keeper's calendar.

harbor_repair_007.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_repair_007.text: It is a better passage, He Ming said. I can admit that without liking your choice best. She bent to examine the corrected fastening, then straightened slowly, protecting her own knee. The road would have brought a reply to somebody who cannot get here, she added. Yue agreed that the need remained. There was no clever answer waiting under the cover. He Ming accepted a cup of water and asked whether the unselected plan would be preserved with its tested costs. The clerk showed her the retained proposal. She wanted the numbers kept, not a promise of money.

harbor_repair_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_008.text: Han came out to see the work near closing time, wearing the sleeve guards she used when ink threatened her cuffs. Deren offered her the safest place to stand. She declined until he pointed out that she was blocking the carrying trial. Her embarrassment made Yan laugh, and his laugh made Deren glance up in surprise. Han inspected the report receiving instructions and said the registry could still improve its existing index within ordinary duties, although the unfunded cabinet could not simply be ordered. She left with a corrected receiving notice under her arm, dry enough to protect her cuffs.

harbor_repair_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_009.text: Deren tried the passage later with an ordinary walking aid and no load. He kept to the recovery advice already given to him. Yan stayed several steps away until Deren asked him to hold a loose door. The request was small enough to fit between everything unresolved. Afterward they ate noodles at separate ends of the same narrow table. Deren's twenty-six copper for missed work had come from his employer's liability payment; it had not purchased this meal or this moment. Yan complained that the noodles had escaped their broth. Deren answered that even noodles deserved a safer passage.

harbor_repair_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_010.text: At the packing room, An and Zhou were binding the third guaranteed batch. Its forty-eight advance was already assigned to materials, space and initial wages; the later balance had not yet been earned. He Ming joined them after inspecting the passage. The private partnership had fourteen copper in reserve following the second completed batch and the earlier two-copper stock purchase. She set that receipt beside her cup, away from the municipal notices. Ke measured a length of wrapping with the confidence of somebody paid for a real task. Nobody asked the traveler to become their unseen fourth purse.

harbor_repair_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_011.text: Peng had adjusted the gull hook with the partners' private payment, and the bird no longer resembled a bent spoon. Its wooden eye still looked affronted. An said it had learned the expression from their landlord. Zhou corrected him: the landlord looked pleased whenever rent was due, whereas the gull seemed to expect a refund. Yue laughed hard enough to spill a little tea, and Ke handed her a rag before the puddle reached a wrapping sheet. They talked about the remaining batches as future work, then moved the clean sheets before starting the bean game.

harbor_repair_012.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_repair_012.text: I borrowed a public room badly once, Han said when she and Yue walked back together. I filled every quiet corner with work because there was space. My own shelf is small enough to make me choose. She asked whether Yue had found a good place for her personal notes. Yue touched the worn notebook in her sleeve. Han warned her against packing damp pages, then admitted she had brought a private sketch to the quay for the light. The drawing showed the corrected cover, a crooked gull and Deren's abandoned noodle bowl. None of it resembled an official plate.

harbor_repair_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_013.text: Luo and Fen received Yue at their own room after supper. Fen had accepted the paid apprenticeship and was making room for its ordinary demands; Luo's lighter records arrangement had its own conditions and hours. The kettle remained their property, along with the stool that leaned unless somebody wedged its leg. Fen asked if the kiln country had the same kind of mud. Yue said she hoped to discover at least one variety she had not already carried indoors. Luo gave her a rag for the road and then reclaimed it, laughing. They both needed it more urgently at home.

harbor_repair_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_014.text: Bao was outside the canteen with Dai when Yue made her last round. Her eighteen copper for lost earnings was a separate employer liability payment, while the warehouse's repair and goods-loss accounts had already closed through their proper returns. She did not want the whole history recited over soup. She wanted Dai to stop choosing the blandest bowl for her. Ke arrived with her personally purchased shears and a story about cutting the wrong wrapping fold, then fixing it before delivery. Wu called them inside to eat. Her canteen stock job continued on its own accepted terms.

harbor_repair_015.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_repair_015.text: The emergency chest still has sixty-eight, Sui told Yue at their farewell, and four unused stones remain secured here. The fragment and spray screen has its established rating. Today's iron does not enlarge it. She closed the cupboard and offered a loaf bought with her own money. Then she admitted that she had wanted the registry option: carrying three versions of an address across a wet yard annoyed her more than she cared to confess. Yue thanked her for saying it. Sui broke off the burnt corner for herself, apparently unwilling to export the evidence of a bad oven.

harbor_repair_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_016.text: Yue settled the end of her seven private lodging nights, already paid fourteen copper from her earned purse, and bought her onward licensed fare separately. Her appointments were closed, all office loans returned. She checked her bedding, cup, personal notes, ordinary blade and wrapped pendant, placing privately purchased road food where she could reach it. No harbor cover, stone, official file or promise of commission went into the pack. Her practice still belonged to the fourth stage, with the same measured expenditure and recovery. She stood from the bed twice to make sure its familiar straps sat comfortably.

harbor_repair_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_repair_017.text: The farewell at the quay happened between ordinary departures. Deren came because his recovery allowed the short visit; Yan came after handing over his assigned work. Han brought no public packet. He Ming was too busy with the third batch to stay long, but she reached the gangway and said she still preferred the road plan. Qin asked Yue to describe the first kiln she actually entered, provided she found a receiving address before sending anything. No companion had been appointed to follow her. The keeper returned to the repair duties as Yue boarded under the boatman's ordinary instructions.

harbor_end_repair.speaker: narrator
harbor_end_repair.text: Six weeks after the harbor's final checks, Yue reached the kiln town as colder weather began. Paid carts, ordinary ferries and stretches on foot had brought her there with her habitual pack, some earned money and the fourth stage she had actually attained. The harbor's later reviews belonged to its accepting officers; she did not claim to have attended them from the road. She remembered Deren's dry joke when a worker pointed out a muddy passage inside the common firing hall. Her visit carried no harbor commission. She asked the local keeper who was taking inquiries about paid work.
harbor_end_repair.ending: A Passage That Holds Its Work

harbor_road_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_001.text: Yue recommended the road plan. She pointed to the tested receiving hours and the difficulty faced by households that could not spend a working day getting to the quay. The committee confirmed the eligible purchase, and its fiscal clerk and contact office route lead countersigned the one sixty-four allocation. Han put away the cabinet quote. Deren folded his drawing with care, leaving it uncreased at the troublesome fastening. The repair proposal remained available for a later decision, without money promised. He Ming looked pleased until the route lead asked her which collecting question should be spoken first.

harbor_road_002.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_road_002.text: Ask whether the person wants to speak now, He Ming said. Then ask what name they want you to use. Don't begin by telling them that you have already found them. She crossed out a florid greeting on the demonstration form and replaced it with a short one. Rong, who had accepted the agreed receiving hours, tried the words aloud until they no longer sounded like a demand for attendance. Yue watched the practice from the table's end. It was the first time that morning He Ming had forgotten to look at her as the chooser of a prize.

harbor_road_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_003.text: The first safe launch day carried two actual collection visits, one assigned worker on each six-copper return fare. The fiscal clerk checked the licensed journeys and receiving times before release. The workers returned that day, rather than treating a return ticket as permission to disappear into another household's evening. Yue did not accompany them as an official inspector. She waited at the receiving desk for the public account of what had been collected. One worker came back with a request for a reply and another with an address correction, each under the person's stated handling permission.

harbor_road_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_004.text: Twelve copper purchased the protected forms used for this bounded launch. They had room for a public reference, the permitted reply route and a plainly separate protected statement. A worker discovered that the folding instruction hid the receiving line when the packet was tied. Han changed the fold before the remaining forms were used. No missing household was forced onto a public list to justify the purchase. The clerk checked the delivered quantity and accepted corrected forms, then paid the quoted twelve. A rejected sample stayed at the desk, where its inconvenient crease was easy to explain.

harbor_road_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_005.text: The twelve-copper interpretation work covered actual collection and reply preparation within the launch. The interpreter read back the intended question, the stated permission and the proposed reply in the required words. A harbor term that meant a work return sounded like a command to return home; the speaker corrected it before the answer was recorded. Rong asked the interpreter to keep the corrected wording with its specific use, rather than pretending the phrase suited every family. The fiscal clerk paid for the completed work after checking the accepted deliveries. Nobody billed a future conversation merely because it might be needed.

harbor_road_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_006.text: On the second safe day, two actual workers carried the prepared replies on the remaining two six-copper return fares. Together the four completed journeys cost twenty-four. The sixteen-copper staff purchase covered the checked collection receiving, preparation and reply tasks performed during the two days. Those accepted costs joined twelve for interpretation and twelve for protected forms: sixty-four spent, zero launch cash left. The contact office keeper retained the receipt packet. The separate four-week review and eight-week closeout remained ordinary assigned responsibilities; their future labor had not been sold as completed work in this launch.

harbor_road_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_007.text: The public reply account was shorter than He Ming expected. It recorded that both permitted reply visits had been made and described the agreed next steps without publishing protected family details. One household accepted its corrected receiving route. Another wanted more time before supplying an additional work paper. No one was declared reunited because a worker had reached a door. He Ming read the account twice, then asked to see where a person could change the permission given during collection. The keeper showed the receiving instruction. Her smile returned, smaller and more useful than it had been during the vote.

harbor_road_008.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_road_008.text: I still prefer the cabinet, Han said while arranging the returned public references. This launch has already made my current shelf busier. She moved the references away from the protected statements, then laughed at herself for finding a fresh complaint inside the success. The tested receiving work had exposed an index omission she could correct within her ordinary duties. The unfunded cabinet order stayed unfunded. She asked Yue to hold a dry public notice while she fastened its corner. When the work was finished, she stepped aside and let a worker read it without explaining what he ought to see.

harbor_road_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_009.text: Deren visited after the carrying work had ended, his aid tapping the boards. He remained disappointed that the checked repair had not been selected. The keeper pointed out the existing fault report and current precautions; choosing the road had not closed that report. Deren made the receiving officer read the date back to him, then sat down. Yan brought tea after his supervised duty and waited to be invited to the neighboring stool. The twenty-six copper for Deren's missed work remained his separate employer liability payment. Their conversation began with the weather and stayed there long enough to become comfortable.

harbor_road_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_010.text: In the private packing room, the partners were partway through the third guaranteed batch. The forty-eight advance had been assigned to its actual materials, space and initial wages; the later balance was still future income. He Ming placed the public reply account outside the wrapping area and joined Zhou at the bench. Their reserve was fourteen after the second completed batch and the earlier two-copper tying-stock purchase. Ke counted the prepared folds for her paid work, while An checked the buyer's actual acceptance conditions. Yue was offered a chair and a cup, without a suggestion that either created an investment.

harbor_road_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_011.text: The gull hook over the bench had improved after Peng's paid private adjustment. Zhou said its beak now pointed toward profitable work. An turned it slightly away from the unfinished batch, saying the bird should not spend money they had not earned. He Ming ordered them both to leave a properly fitted hook alone. They obeyed until she turned to fetch the supper cups, then looked at each other with the same guilty grin. Yue lost the bean game because she watched that grin instead of the board. Wu came from her separate canteen stock work and demanded a rematch.

harbor_road_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_012.text: Fen and Luo brought their own supper contributions to the farewell table, leaving the household kettle at home. Fen's accepted paid apprenticeship had become a subject she could discuss without asking for permission in every sentence. Luo described the lighter records hours he had agreed, then admitted he still worried about tiring before the last task. The others let her say both things. Ke offered to carry a heavy bundle the following day only after checking his own paid shift. They went home arguing cheerfully about the best use of a free morning.

harbor_road_013.speaker: harbor_qin_shuo
harbor_road_013.text: The journey will be ordinary and badly described, Qin told Yue. People call a road easy because they have never taken it with your pack. He had bought a paper of beans with his own money and was trying to divide it without dropping any through the bench slats. His approved shorter role had coverage and ordinary employer pay; it had not become part of the pilot's staff purchase. He offered Yue the less burnt handful. Then he asked her to remember the names of useful inns, a request practical enough to survive the foolish way he had made it.

harbor_road_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_014.text: Bao and Dai found Yue near the canteen door. Bao's eighteen-copper lost-earnings payment had come from the separate warehouse employer liability account; it did not make every future difficulty settled. She was interested in a manageable task when her recovery allowed it and said so without asking the traveler to promise one. Ke showed Dai the shears bought from her own money and described the cut she had learned to avoid. Wu called them away from the doorway because they were blocking the customers. The interruption pleased Bao, who said she wanted to be scolded for ordinary inconvenience again.

harbor_road_015.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_road_015.text: We keep sixty-eight in the emergency allocation and four unused stones here, Sui said while locking the store. The screen remains rated for fragment and spray protection. A paid journey does not make a boat immune to weather. She looked up to check that Yue was smiling for the right reason, then offered a privately bought loaf. Her preferred plan had been the registry, and she said it without expecting a second vote. Yue thanked her for the bread and the care. Sui took back the cloth wrapping, which belonged to the canteen, before Yue could accidentally pack it.

harbor_road_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_016.text: The seven private lodging nights ended with their fourteen-copper bed payment already made from Yue's earned purse. She paid her ordinary onward fare separately and checked the food she had bought for travel. Her bedding, cup, personal notes, ordinary blade and wrapped pendant fitted the habitual pack; all office loans and protected working files stayed returned. No boat fare from the completed pilot followed her onto the road. She practiced one short measured fourth-stage exercise, rested afterward and repacked a strap that pinched. She was leaving with familiar limits, tired feet and a curiosity that had outlasted them.

harbor_road_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_road_017.text: He Ming reached the departure berth carrying only her own cup from the workroom. She thanked Yue for choosing the route and then admitted she would have argued at her farewell if she had chosen otherwise. Han said that was fortunate, because she still intended to argue. Deren waved from the safer bench beside Yan. Fen had an apprenticeship task, Luo her accepted hours, Wu her canteen work and the partners their unfinished third batch. None was assigned to follow. The boatman called the actual boarding order, and Yue stepped aboard with her pack rather than a harbor office.

harbor_end_road.speaker: narrator
harbor_end_road.text: Six weeks after the final harbor checks, paid carts, ferries and walking brought Yue to the kiln town as cold weather began. She carried her habitual personal pack, earned money and the fourth stage she had earned, without borrowed harbor equipment or a promised commission. The contact office's later reviews belonged to its accepting staff; the traveler had not performed them while absent. A worker inside the common firing hall asked where she had come from. Yue answered with the harbor's ordinary name, then asked who locally received inquiries about paid work and a place to stay.
